description: Recommends early procurement for 60% of 2027-2028 road, sidewalk work.
This two-year pilot aims to improve project delivery and secure better bids.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Early procurement for up to 60% of 2027-2028 program funding.
Councillors praised early procurement for potential cost savings and efficiency.
City taxpayers could save money through competitive bidding.
Two-year pilot to evaluate early procurement process.
Construction Association of Saskatchewan supports early procurement.

description: New rules for Link BRT transit signals and lanes.
Prohibits unauthorized vehicles from dedicated transit lanes.
Updates bus stop definitions and stopping rules.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Councillor raised concerns about SGI approval and potential provincial traffic act conflicts.
Drivers and visitors will need to learn new transit signal rules.
Councillor flagged potential legal risks with provincial Traffic Act amendments.

description: City terminates poor-performing winter road maintenance contracts.
One contractor was terminated, ineligible to bid until 2029.
Administration opposes rotating contractors between service areas.

chips.text: Councillor Dunner emphasized "best value" over lowest price for contracts.
Residents in Area 2 and Area 4 experienced contractor issues.
City can suspend suppliers for significant or persistent deficiencies.
Using past performance in bids requires careful, defensible procurement.
Staff committed to continuously refining and improving the process.

description: City will not coordinate priority street snow grading with waste collection.
Administration will track complaints and document current practices.

chips.text: Few residents are directly impacted by current priority street grading practices.
Resident surveys show high satisfaction with waste collection; no complaints found in 5 years.

description: Provides information and research on taxi by-law amendments.
Discussion continues on driver safety and upfront taxi fares.
Administration will report back by early next year.

chips.text: Saskatoon taxi drivers are directly impacted by these changes.
Taxi union welcomes safety discussion, but not mandatory shields due to cost.
Administration will report back on taxi by-law amendments by early next year.

speakers.name: Malik Draz
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Taxi Items
said: Union welcomes driver safety discussions; encourages voluntary safety shield installation.
Does not recommend mandatory safety shields due to significant cost.
Appreciates initial report's decision to collect fares upfront.

description: Sets large taxi fare at $9.50 when passenger requests it.
Requires taxi brokerages to supply all driver equipment.
Removes driver discretion for charging large vehicle fares.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
One driver has a debit machine lease until October 2027, costing $30/month.
Administration stated bylaws are not for one-off situations like a single driver's lease.
USW local 2014 opposed new large vehicle rates, citing reduced driver income.
Administration will work with one driver and brokerage on debit machine lease solution.

description: City explores better snow removal near senior complexes.
Aims to improve accessibility for seniors, emergency services.
Three options presented: windrow, priority network, new service.
Council direction needed for cost estimates.

chips.text: Councillor questioned why resident and councillor-reported issues were excluded from data.
60 high-density senior complexes and emergency services are affected.
Administration will refine snow grading practices for senior complexes.

description: Many city crosswalks do not meet current safety standards.
Pedestrians, especially vulnerable groups, face danger.
Administration needs five more years to update all signals.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Updating signals is complex, requiring physical changes for some intersections.
Seniors, children, and people with mobility challenges are most affected.
Staff do not prioritize crosswalk updates over major road planning.
Administration has not scanned other cities' progress on crosswalk updates.
Over 85 petition respondents reported feeling rushed and unsafe.

speakers.name: Zachary De Francesco
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Addressing Substandard Signalized Crosswalk Times
said: Many signalized crosswalks have substandard crossing times, making them unsafe.
A case study showed a 30-meter crosswalk provides 26 seconds, but TAC requires 30.
City should create a plan to audit and update all intersections to meet TAC standards.

description: City can boot vehicles on private property for unpaid parking fines.
Outstanding parking fines reduced to $6.6 million.
Administration to report on fine collection strategy in Q4.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Individuals with unpaid parking judgments are subject to vehicle immobilization.
Correspondence from Lionel Katchmar raised concerns about parking enforcement and debt collection.
